page: Google Cloud Platform m2-hypermem-416 is a memory-optimized server instance designed for large-scale in-memory workloads. It features 416 vCPUs mapped to 208 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.7 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 8.625 TB of RAM, yielding approximately 21.23 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Conversely, multi-core and parallelized execution are highly efficient; the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU score, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression all rank in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached reads and writes placing in the top 10%. However, Passmark memory scores are in the bottom 25%, indicating potential latency or architectural overheads in specific synthetic memory tests despite the massive bandwidth.

Given the massive memory footprint and high multi-threaded throughput, this instance is suited for large in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, and complex data-processing pipelines. It is less suited for single-threaded tasks or LLM text generation, where it exhibits poor performance. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high resource density of 8.625 TB RAM on a single node reduces the need for distributed cluster management, though the premium hardware class represents a significant resource commitment.
